input: Teamwork is useful because people have different skills.
question: Why is teamwork useful?

feedback.final_upgraded_answer: Teamwork is useful because people bring different skills to the table.
feedback.reference_answer: I'd say teamwork is useful less for what it adds and more for what it prevents. When you work alone, there's nobody to challenge your assumptions, so small mistakes can quietly grow into big ones. In a team, though, someone usually notices when something doesn't add up, and that early catch saves a lot of trouble later. I've seen this in part-time jobs — one person misses a detail, another spots it before it reaches the customer. So the real value isn't just extra hands; it's having a natural check on your own blind spots. That said, it only works if people feel comfortable speaking up. If everyone just agrees to keep the peace, you lose that safety net entirely.
feedback.reference_angle_summary: 独立主线：团队合作的价值在于“预防错误”而非“增加产出”，强调早期纠错与心理安全的条件；示例不代表用户经历。

feedback.reference_answer: I'd say teamwork is useful mainly because it lets people cover each other's weak spots. Nobody's good at everything, so when you work with others, you can lean on their strengths and they can lean on yours. For example, in a group project, one person might be great at planning while another is better at actually getting things done, and together they produce something neither could manage alone. It also takes some pressure off you, because you're not carrying the whole thing by yourself. That said, teamwork only works if people actually communicate, otherwise it just turns into confusion. So for me, the real value is that it turns a bunch of individual skills into something bigger than the sum of its parts.

feedback.reference_answer: For me, the real usefulness of teamwork shows up when a problem is too big or too messy for one person to even see clearly. A single person tends to get stuck in their own way of thinking, but once you put three or four heads together, someone usually spots the angle you completely missed. I noticed this when a friend's small business was losing customers — she kept blaming the product, but her staff pointed out it was actually the slow replies to messages. That's something she'd never have seen alone. So teamwork isn't just about sharing the workload; it's about catching each other's blind spots. Of course, that only works if people feel safe enough to speak up, otherwise you just get one voice and a lot of nodding.
